newsitem.title: UK: Bank of Scotland up after Sainsbury move.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Scotland up after Sainsbury move.

text.p: Shares in Bank of Scotland firmed in early trading Monday after last week's announcement of a banking joint venture with J Sainsbury drew a positive response from industry analysts.

Market sources said SBC Warburg had upgraded its recommendation on the stock to "trading buy" from "hold" while Goldman Sachs and BZW reitereated their positive stances on the group. By late morning the shares had added 4p to 287p.
"The Sainsbury move is a confirmation of Bank of Scotland's strategy of alternative distribution into England," said Goldman's David Townshend.
"Unlike other UK banks it has no cannibalisation implications and so is a straightforward positive. It shows its strategy is consistent, sensible and the group is very undervalued."
The new bank will begin operating in the first half of 1997, starting with credit cards and deposits. Eventually the product range will include lending and other savings products.
